title: Move unreadCount to ChatMessagePush
description:
Oracle: jmap-chat-spec 6bcd9d8 (quoted text). Mapped by wf_6712c4f8-c2b.

[chat-ext] Move unreadCount from ChatMessageEntry to ChatMessagePush
Spec (db880a1): draft-atwood-jmap-chat-push-00.md L149-150 (in the ChatMessagePush object): "`unreadCount` (UnsignedInt|null, optional): : The account owner's total unread message count across all non-muted Chats at the time this push was generated. ... It is a property of the push as a whole, not of any one entry, and is not governed by the `properties` list of {{chat-push-config}}." (removed from the ChatMessageEntry field list)
Code: crate-jmap-chat-types/src/push.rs:161-167 ChatMessageEntry.unread_count; crate-jmap-chat-types/src/push.rs:194-205 ChatMessagePush (no unread_count); crate-jmap-chat-types/src/push.rs:222-227 ChatMessagePushFields twin and Serialize impl; crate-jmap-chat-types/src/push.rs:330,362 (constructors); crate-jmap-chat-types/src/push.rs:640-655 (unit test asserting entry-level unreadCount); crate-jmap-chat-server/src/push.rs:30 and :401 (docs)
Now: unreadCount is typed on each entry. A conformant payload's top-level unreadCount lands in ChatMessagePush.extra, and an entry-level value we emit is not where receivers look.
Change: Add `unread_count: Option<u64>` to ChatMessagePush and its twin (wire `unreadCount`, skip if None), and remove it from ChatMessageEntry. Update the constructors, docs, and the unit test oracle to L149. ENTRY_PROPERTIES already excludes it, which is correct.
